experiment: Stage 2.9 baseline iterative deepening under wall-clock budgets
hypothesis: Iterative deepening can return the deepest fully completed Baseline A search inside a practical wall-clock budget while every completed iteration remains action- and search-tree-equivalent to the corresponding fixed-depth baseline search.
interpretation: All 86 tests passed before the benchmark, including deterministic tests that completed iterative depths preserve Baseline A actions and expanded-node counts and that an incomplete first iteration is discarded rather than treated as authoritative.

Across all four budgets and all 16 frozen CLSN1 positions, every fully completed iterative depth matched the corresponding fixed-depth Baseline A action and search-node count exactly. No budget required the depth-0 fallback.
At 50 ms, 14 of 16 positions completed depth 2, one completed depth 3, and one completed depth 4; mean completed depth was 2.19.

At 150 ms, 15 of 16 positions completed depth 3 and one completed depth 4; mean completed depth was 3.06. This makes roughly 150 ms the first measured budget that delivers depth-3 Baseline A essentially across the whole frozen suite.
At 500 ms, 14 of 16 positions completed depth 4 and two completed depth 3; the two depth-3 cases were standard-start Game 2 and full-spread Game 2. Mean completed depth was 3.88.
At 1000 ms, all 16 positions completed depth 4. The slowest full iterative-deepening decision observed was 721.08 ms, so the 1 s budget had substantial headroom on this CI runner.

Deadline checks behaved as intended: maximum observed overrun was 0.57 ms at the tested budgets. This is a soft Python deadline rather than a hard real-time guarantee, but the current check granularity is sufficiently tight for the experiment.

The next isolated experiment should run the same budgets and frozen positions with the previously validated CLSN-equivalent structural exact transposition table, preserving the same completed-depth equivalence checks. The question is whether search reuse converts the same wall-clock budgets into reliably deeper completed searches.
